finding.claim: Default SCP remote-path transform (DoubleQuote) escapes only double quotes, so $(...), backticks and backslash sequences in an application-supplied path are interpreted by the remote shell, giving remote command injection.
finding.source: Remote path or filename string supplied by the calling application (e.g. user-chosen upload/download path). Default transform is DoubleQuote (ScpClient.cs:159-163).
finding.sink: ScpClient.cs:578 (and 367, 410, 459, 498, 538) builds 'scp -f {Transform(filename)}' passed to channel.SendExecRequest, executed by the remote shell.

trace.note: Download builds scp -f with Transform(filename), no further quoting
Wraps in double quotes; only embedded '"' gets a backslash prefix
Backslashes and $, backtick are not escaped, so $(cmd) expands in remote shell

finding.guards_checked: Only embedded double quotes are escaped. $, backtick and backslash are not. A backslash before an embedded quote also breaks out because the backslash itself is not doubled. The ShellQuote transform exists (RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation.cs) but its implementation was not verified.

finding.claim: Host key trust defaults to accept: with no HostKeyReceived subscriber CanTrustHostKey returns true, and HostKeyEventArgs.CanTrust defaults to true, so a MITM with any validly-signed key is trusted unless the application explicitly rejects it.
finding.source: Network attacker on the path to the SSH server presenting its own host key.
finding.sink: Trust decision authenticating the server before client credentials are sent (KeyExchange.cs:493 ValidateExchangeHash returns VerifySignature && CanTrustHostKey).

trace.note: Signature verification only proves possession of the presented key
Returns true when no HostKeyReceived handler is subscribed
Constructor sets CanTrust = true, so a handler that only logs fingerprints trusts every host

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification of exchange hash is present. No known-hosts or pinning default. CertificateHostAlgorithm.cs:118-150 checks validity period and CA signature but not certificate principals against the target hostname; CA trust and hostname matching are left to the caller.

finding.claim: HTTP CONNECT request line is built from unvalidated Host and Port; CR/LF or spaces in Host let an attacker inject proxy request headers or a second request.
finding.source: Host string from ConnectionInfo, attacker-controlled when the application takes the SSH host from user input and an HTTP proxy is configured.
finding.sink: Request line 'CONNECT {host}:{port} HTTP/1.0' written to the proxy socket (HttpConnector.cs:61-64).

trace.note: Host only checked for non-empty; no CR/LF or character validation
Formatted unescaped into CONNECT request line

finding.guards_checked: Proxy credentials are Base64-encoded (HttpConnector.cs:71) and are safe. Port is validated numerically via ValidatePort(); the host is not validated.

finding.claim: Server DH public value f (and group-exchange p/g) is not range- or structure-checked before use in shared-secret computation, allowing degenerate shared secrets.
finding.source: Server-sent KEXDH_REPLY F value and, for group exchange, server-chosen prime p and generator g.

trace.note: DHParameters built from server p and g with no primality or generator check

finding.guards_checked: No 1 < f < p-1 check, primality, or generator check found in the Security folder. Exploitation requires a MITM that is also trusted, so this is defence in depth.
